 Myntra Beauty Adds Korean Skincare Brand Anua to Its Portfolio 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor
 Oct 27, 2026 
 Oct 27, 2026 / 
 146 
 / 4 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 -->
 -->
 Myntra Beauty has added Korean skincare brand Anua to its portfolio as it expands its selection of international beauty labels in India. The brand focuses on ingredient-led formulations and skincare routines designed to address specific skin concerns. 
 Anua's debut on the platform includes 16 stock-keeping units (SKUs) across serums, face washes, cleansers and facial sunscreens. With this addition, Myntra Beauty's Korean beauty portfolio comprises approximately 100 brands, following the recent inclusion of Frankly and Seapuri. 
 Anua offers products targeting skin concerns such as sensitivity, redness, blemishes, uneven skin tone, and dehydration. Its selection on Myntra Beauty includes the Heartleaf Cleansing Oil and Azelaic Acid 10 Hyaluron Redness Soothing Serum with Cica. 
 The brand's offerings are divided into two key ranges. The Heartleaf range is formulated for sensitive and reactive skin, while the Peach & Rice range focuses on brightening and nourishment. Its wider portfolio includes products formulated with ingredients such as PDRN, niacinamide, tranexamic acid (TXA), azelaic acid, hyaluronic acid, retinol, vitamin C, ceramides and beta hydroxy acid (BHA). The range also includes sun protection products. 
 Deepak Joshi, Senior Director – Category Management, Beauty and Personal Care, Myntra said , "India's beauty consumer is increasingly intentional about ingredients, routines and outcomes, and that's exactly the audience we've been building Myntra Beauty's K-Beauty portfolio for. The launch of Anua is a step towards further curating a destination where skincare enthusiasts can discover the next big K-Beauty brand and the ones they already love. Anua's balance of gentle daily care and targeted solutions makes it a standout addition to that mix." 
 Kevin Hyun, Global Sales & Business Development Leader, Anua shared , "Anua has built its global journey around skincare that is gentle, effective and responsive to real consumer concerns. India is an exciting beauty market, with consumers becoming more aware of ingredients, skin routines and targeted care. Through Myntra Beauty’s widespread reach across India and its diverse customer base, we're pleased to make our portfolio across calming, brightening, hydrating and focused skincare solutions more accessible to Indian consumers." 
 The addition of Anua also expands Myntra's international brand selection, which includes more than 20,000 styles from over 360 global brands across categories. The platform continues to broaden its beauty portfolio amid rising interest in ingredient-focused skincare and international beauty brands among Indian consumers.

 Snapdeal Parent AceVector Sees Revenue Growth and Higher Losses in Q2 FY27 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 27, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 AceVector, the parent company of e-commerce marketplace Snapdeal, reported a 17 percent year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 151.2 crore in Q2 FY27, marking its first quarterly results since its stock market listing earlier this month. However, the company’s net loss increased 85 percent to Rs 17.6 crore.  
 AceVector's operating revenue stood at Rs 129.3 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Including Rs 2.6 crore in non-operating income, its total income reached Rs 153.8 crore during the quarter. 
 Snapdeal's marketplace business contributed Rs 86.2 crore, accounting for 57 percent of operating revenue and registering 15 percent year-on-year growth. Unicommerce, AceVector's e-commerce enablement software-as-a-service (SaaS) platform, generated Rs 59 crore, while its consumer brands business contributed Rs 6 crore. 
 For the first half of FY27, AceVector's consolidated revenue increased 17 percent year-on-year to Rs 285.5 crore. Snapdeal's revenue rose 15 percent to Rs 164.4 crore, while Unicommerce recorded a similar 15 percent increase to Rs 110.4 crore. 
 Snapdeal's fashion net merchandise value (NMV) grew 31 percent year-on-year to Rs 407.6 crore in H1 FY27. Its annual transacting customer base increased 12 percent to 130.8 lakh, while app-delivered units rose 23 percent to 133.6 lakh. During the period, the marketplace also introduced an artificial intelligence (AI) solutions suite offering features for product discovery, personalised recommendations, and seller support. 
 AceVector's total expenditure increased more than 21 percent to Rs 168.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 138.7 crore a year earlier. Logistics remained its largest expense at Rs 71.4 crore, up 20 percent year-on-year, while employee benefit expenses stood at Rs 46 crore. The reported loss included Rs 1.3 crore in exceptional items. 
 AceVector's Rs 420 crore initial public offering (IPO) received approximately five times subscription but made a weak stock market debut. Shares listed at an 11.5 percent discount to the IPO price of Rs 32, opening at Rs 28.32 on the NSE and Rs 28.30 on the BSE. 
 The IPO comprised a fresh issue of Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale of Rs 133 crore, with a price band of Rs 30 to Rs 32 per share. At Monday's market close, AceVector shares stood at Rs 20.92, giving the company a market capitalisation of Rs 1,138 crore.

 Swiss Beauty Makes Paris Fashion Week Debut with Eight Makeup Looks 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 26, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Swiss Beauty, an Indian cosmetics brand, has partnered with Paris Fashion Week to showcase its makeup products on the international runway. As part of the association, the brand created eight makeup looks using its products, featured on six models and two influencers.
 The partnership marks a step in Swiss Beauty’s efforts to expand its presence beyond India and strengthen its association with the global fashion and beauty industry. The collaboration brings the brand’s products into the runway creative process, positioning makeup as an integral part of fashion presentation and self-expression.
 According to the company, the initiative reflects its ambition to explore new platforms for showcasing its products beyond conventional marketing and consumer engagement channels.
 Commenting on the association, Mohit, Founder, Swiss Beauty, said the brand’s participation at Paris Fashion Week represents an important milestone in its growth journey and reflects its ambitions for the future.
 He added that the platform offers the brand an opportunity to take its makeup expertise to an international fashion audience.
 Swiss Beauty Focuses on Creative Makeup and Global Exposure 
 The eight runway looks were designed to highlight the versatility of Swiss Beauty’s products across different styles and creative expressions. The brand said the initiative allowed its products to become part of the show's creative process rather than serving solely as a branding element.
 Shalini, AVP – Marketing, Swiss Beauty, said the partnership was significant because the brand’s products were used to develop the runway looks. She added that the eight looks demonstrated different applications of its makeup range and reflected the brand’s focus on self-expression.
 The collaboration also brought Swiss Beauty’s brand philosophy, “We Got You”, to an international fashion platform.
 Gresha Sen Gupta, AVP – Creative Director, Swiss Beauty, said the association was an opportunity to connect fashion and beauty in a new setting. She added that the brand aimed to demonstrate its creative approach through different faces, looks and runway presentations.
 Expanding Beyond Traditional Beauty Marketing 
 Swiss Beauty worked with Gold Coast to bring the partnership to life at Paris Fashion Week. The initiative forms part of the brand’s broader strategy to take its products beyond conventional brand and consumer touchpoints and into global fashion and cultural platforms.
 By integrating its makeup products into a runway presentation, the brand aims to strengthen its positioning at the intersection of beauty, fashion and creative expression while reaching an international audience.

 Myntra Big Fashion Festival Sees Nearly 2X Orders for D2C Brands 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 26, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Myntra’s Big Fashion Festival (BFF) recorded nearly double the order volume of regular business days for direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, international labels, and its Gen Z-focused fashion platform FWD, according to the company. The event also expanded the reach of emerging brands, with visits increasing 25 percent compared with the previous edition and new customers from non-metro regions rising 74 percent over regular business days. 
 Several Indian and international brands recorded strong demand during the fashion sale. These included RARE RABBIT, House of Pataudi, Glitchez, The Souled Store, SZN, CULT, Comet, Mamaearth and Minimalist. International brands that saw traction included MANGO, H&M, NEXT, Mothercare, ALDO, GAP, GUESS, Michael Kors, Fossil, Gymshark, Women's Secret, adidas and Nike.
 Myntra has onboarded 12,000 sellers so far in 2026, giving emerging businesses from cities such as Surat, Ludhiana, Kolkata and Delhi-NCR access to customers across India. During the Big Fashion Festival, one in four sellers recorded a twofold increase in sales, while more than 1,350 sellers reported a fivefold rise. 
 Non-metro markets contributed to customer acquisition during the event, with Guwahati, Dehradun, Bhubaneswar, Jammu and Gorakhpur emerging as the fastest-growing non-metro cities. Traffic on the first day also recorded a significant year-on-year increase, while men's casual wear accounted for 26 percent of all first-time buyers.
 Festive shopping demand in eastern India, particularly West Bengal, Assam and Odisha, was higher than during the previous edition. Ethnic wear, footwear and beauty and personal care products contributed to the increase. Ethnic wear brands that recorded demand included Libas, Inddus, Soch, Koski and Aurelia.
 Men's occasion wear, men's casual footwear, wearables, sports footwear, watches, eyewear, women's sports apparel, jewellery, luggage, travel and accessories were among the fastest-growing categories. Sports footwear orders increased 3.5 times compared with regular business days. Men's casual wear, personal care, women's ethnic wear, women's western wear and kidswear were among the categories with the highest demand.
 Myntra Beauty also recorded an increase in customer acquisition, with new customers rising about 20 percent compared with the previous edition. Perfumes, face washes, cleansers, day creams and lipsticks were among the leading product categories. Brands including Lakme, Mamaearth, L'Oréal, Maybelline and Cetaphil recorded strong demand. 
 Myntra's quick-commerce service, M-Now, recorded more than 2.6 times growth in orders compared with the previous Big Fashion Festival. Demand included kurta sets, T-shirts, shirts, tops, jeans, dresses, perfumes, lipsticks, sarees, lingerie and watches. Brands recording high demand on M-Now included MANGO, Allen Solly, USPA, Van Heusen, Trendyol, Puma, Underneath, Anouk, Sangria, HRX, Maybelline, Lakme and Minimalist.
 The fastest M-Now delivery during the event took less than five minutes. The most expensive purchase was an international luxury jacket valued at more than Rs 1,90,000. The latest edition of the Big Fashion Festival highlighted demand across fashion, beauty, sportswear and lifestyle categories, while providing emerging sellers with access to a wider customer base through Myntra's online marketplace.

 Rajesh Pratap Singh Expands PRATAP Into Home Furnishings 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 26, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Fashion designer Rajesh Pratap Singh has introduced PRATAP HOME, a home textiles and lifestyle objects label that extends his design practice into the home decor market. The launch follows 29 years of the PRATAP label’s work in craft-led clothing and design. PRATAP HOME brings the label’s focus on materials, craftsmanship and functional design to home furnishings and interior products. The collection includes textiles, lighting, rugs, table linen, decorative objects, tiles and wall art, with an emphasis on handcrafted details and practical use. 
 The Bed and Table range features hand-quilted and block-printed quilts, dohars, cushions and shams. The products incorporate details such as pintucks, jacquard weaving, embroidery and block printing. The collection also includes woven, printed and embroidered table linen, along with hand-knotted and flat-woven rugs in different patterns and colours. The label has also introduced window sheers designed to add texture and subtle patterns to interior spaces. The range brings together different textile techniques and materials across bedroom, dining and living areas.
 PRATAP HOME’s Light and Objects category includes candles, candle stands, custom lighting and chandeliers made using materials such as metal, glass and wood. The designs combine sculptural elements with everyday functionality. The collection also extends to interior surfaces and wall decor through signature tiles developed in collaboration with FCML, alongside a selection of wall art. Together, the product categories mark the brand’s entry into home furnishings and interior lifestyle products.
 Rajesh Pratap Singh said, " I did not design for a particular kind of interior. I designed for a way of living. These pieces belong in spaces that have room to breathe, where every object is there for a reason and nothing is there to impress. "
 PRATAP HOME extends the designer’s work beyond apparel into products for different areas of the home. The collection brings together textiles, lighting and decorative elements under the same design approach used by the clothing label. The collection is available at the PRATAP store in Kala Ghoda, Mumbai, and through the brand’s official website, https://rajeshpratapsingh.com/.

 Senco Gold to Acquire 68 Pc Stake in Melorra for Rs 68 Cr 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 26, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Senco Gold Ltd has agreed to acquire a 68 percent stake in August Jewellery Pvt Ltd, the company behind the Melorra jewellery brand, for Rs 68 crore. The transaction is expected to close by February 2027, subject to the fulfilment of specified conditions.
 The investment will be completed in multiple tranches through the issuance of fresh equity shares. The proceeds will be used to fund August Jewellery’s growth and expansion plans and settle its existing liabilities. After the transaction, Senco Gold and an entity belonging to its promoter group will jointly hold a 79 percent stake in August Jewellery, making it a subsidiary of Senco Gold. 
 The acquisition aligns with Senco Gold’s digital and omnichannel expansion strategy, particularly its efforts to connect with younger consumers. Melorra’s design capabilities and e-commerce operations are expected to complement Senco Gold’s existing business and support operational efficiencies and customer experience across online and offline channels.
 August Jewellery operates in the gold, silver and precious-stone jewellery segment through Melorra, which focuses on lightweight, fast-fashion jewellery. The brand operates 20 stores across India and uses technology to develop and introduce new designs every week. August Jewellery reported a turnover of Rs 97.93 crore in the financial year ended March 31, 2026. Its turnover stood at Rs 33.25 crore in FY2024-25, compared with Rs 173.63 crore in FY2023-24.

 Wow! Momo Plans QSR Entry into Sri Lanka, Eyes UAE and US Markets 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 26, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Wow! Momo Foods is expanding beyond India as it looks to establish its quick-service restaurant (QSR) business in international markets while growing its packaged food portfolio overseas. The company plans to launch its first international QSR operations in Sri Lanka, while Wow! FMCG, which currently exports to 14 countries, is targeting the US, Malaysia, Australia, Thailand and Canada for further expansion. 
 The Sri Lanka entry will be undertaken through a master franchise partnership with Softlogic Corporation, a diversified Sri Lankan conglomerate. The company plans to open its first three outlets in Colombo across different formats, including Wow! Momo Asia at One Galle Face Mall, a food court outlet at Havelock City Mall and a standalone restaurant at Arcade Independence Square. 
 Wow! Momo Foods aims to expand its Sri Lankan network to 20 outlets within the first two years. The launch will also help the company understand local consumer preferences and develop an operating model for future international expansion. 
 “When you build a brand in India, you naturally start wondering whether the same love for the product can travel beyond the country. But going global is not about assuming that what works here will automatically work everywhere. It is about listening, learning and adapting,” said Sagar Daryani, Co-founder and CEO, Wow! Momo Foods Pvt. Ltd. 
 UAE Next on QSR Roadmap 
 Following Sri Lanka, the company is evaluating the UAE as its next international QSR market, with Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah under consideration. It is in discussions with potential partners and exploring joint venture and master franchise arrangements. 
 The US is also on the company's roadmap, with entry targeted after the next two years. The experience gained in Sri Lanka and the UAE is expected to help the company determine suitable menus, formats and partnerships before entering the market. 
 FMCG Business in 14 Countries 
 While its restaurant business prepares for its first international entry, Wow! FMCG has already established an overseas presence across 14 countries, including the UAE, Oman, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Russia, Singapore, the UK, Ireland, Germany, Mauritius, Sri Lanka and New Zealand. 
 Its portfolio includes momos, noodles, cup noodles, smileys and kulfi, distributed through more than 1,000 international touchpoints across modern retail and e-commerce. 
 The FMCG business has partnered with LuLu Group International to expand its presence in the Middle East and other retail channels. It also works with Noon and Amazon Middle East, while Mustafa Centre serves as a retail partner in Singapore. Its products are also supplied to international restaurants, cafes, catering businesses and commercial kitchens. 
 “Our FMCG journey has been built market by market, with a strong focus on understanding local consumer behaviour, building the right distribution partnerships and creating a portfolio that can scale across diverse markets,” said Mithun Appaiah, CEO, Wow! Sales Pvt. Ltd. 
 He added that the next phase would focus on entering new geographies, strengthening distribution in existing markets and expanding the company's retail, e-commerce and foodservice network. 
 The company is also in discussions with large international retail chains to widen its distribution. Its FMCG business is currently entirely focused on branded retail, reflecting its strategy of building consumer recognition across markets. 
 Founded in 2008 , Wow! Momo Foods has grown from a single kiosk into a multi-brand business with more than 900 stores across over 100 Indian cities . Its portfolio includes Wow! Momo, Wow! China, Wow! Chicken and Wow! Kulfi. The planned overseas expansion marks its next step towards building an international presence across restaurant and packaged food businesses.

 HomeLane Targets Rs 1,000 Cr Revenue in FY27 After Turning EBITDA Positive in Q4 FY26 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 26, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 HomeLane, a technology-enabled home interiors company, is targeting revenue of more than ₹1,000 crore in FY27 after achieving operating EBITDA profitability in the fourth quarter of FY26. The company reported quarterly revenue of ₹212 crore and an operating EBITDA margin of 5% in Q4 FY26.
 The company has also reported strong business momentum in the first half of FY27, with revenue growing 19% year on year and its order book increasing 37%, according to unaudited management figures.
 HomeLane expects the growth in its order book to support revenue performance in the second half of FY27, as orders typically convert into revenue over the following six to nine months. Backed by a leaner cost structure and a growing project pipeline, the company is targeting full-year EBITDA profitability in FY27.
 HomeLane Improves Project Margins After Integration 
 FY26 marked the first full financial year of HomeLane and DesignCafe operating together. During the year, the company prioritised integrating the two businesses over accelerating revenue growth, with revenue remaining stable at ₹745 crore.
 The integration helped improve project economics, with direct project costs declining from 56.6% of revenue in FY25 to 52% in FY26. This 460-basis-point improvement was driven by the consolidation of sourcing, manufacturing partners and installation operations across the two brands.
 HomeLane has also completed the amalgamation of G S E-Commerce Private Limited, which operates DesignCafe, into Homevista Decor and Furnishings Private Limited, the group's parent company. The business now operates as a single legal entity with HomeLane and DesignCafe continuing as separate consumer brands, supported by a common technology platform, supply chain and operating infrastructure.
 Loss Narrows on a Like-for-Like Basis 
 HomeLane reported a loss before tax of ₹137 crore in FY26, compared with ₹111 crore in FY25. The FY26 figure included ₹19 crore in integration-related and one-time costs.
 Excluding these expenses and other one-off items, the company's loss before tax stood at ₹118 crore in FY26, broadly in line with the previous financial year.
 Commenting on the company's performance, Srikanth Iyer, Co-founder and CEO, HomeLane, said the integration of HomeLane and DesignCafe was a priority during FY26, helping improve project economics and achieve operating EBITDA profitability in the fourth quarter.
 He added that the company has returned to growth in FY27, with revenue increasing 19% and the order book expanding 37% year on year in the first half. HomeLane is now focused on crossing ₹1,000 crore in revenue and achieving full-year EBITDA profitability, with support from its teams and franchise partners.

 Supersox Strengthens Offline Presence with Vashi Kiosk Launch 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 24, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Supersox India has expanded its retail presence with the opening of a new kiosk at Inorbit Mall in Vashi, Navi Mumbai, as the socks brand looks to make its products more accessible to consumers across India. 
 The new kiosk offers Supersox’s range of socks, including printed designs and everyday essentials. The collection focuses on combining comfort with colorful designs, catering to consumers looking to add variety to their everyday wardrobe. 
 The latest opening adds to the brand’s retail expansion efforts, with Supersox looking to establish a presence at more consumer destinations across the country. The company has indicated that it plans to expand to additional locations, although it has not announced specific details of its upcoming openings. 
 The kiosk at Inorbit Mall, Vashi, provides customers with access to the brand’s range through a physical retail format, allowing shoppers to explore its collection in person.

 Geetanjali Salon Opens New Flagship in Chandigarh, Partners with Kérastase 
 BY - Indian Retailer Bureau 
 Sub Editor 
 Oct 24, 2026 
 / 1 MIN READ 
 Follow Us 
 Geetanjali Salon, a 37-year-old beauty brand, has expanded its presence in Chandigarh with the launch of a new flagship salon in Sector 9. The launch was attended by actress Jasmin Bhasin, marking another addition to the brand’s salon network. 
 The new flagship will feature Kérastase as its haircare partner, bringing professional haircare and beauty services to customers in the city. The partnership adds a premium haircare offering to the salon’s service portfolio. 
 The Chandigarh launch marks the brand’s continued presence in the beauty and salon services market, where professional treatments and premium haircare offerings remain important parts of the consumer experience. With the new flagship, Geetanjali Salon aims to strengthen its presence in Chandigarh while offering customers access to professional salon services and specialized haircare solutions. 
 Commenting on the launch, Jasmin Bhasin said, “I have been a regular client of Geetanjali for many years, so it feels amazing to be part of yet another launch, especially in Chandigarh. Being here for this milestone feels truly special. With the brand looking to expand across the Tricity, it’s exciting to see Geetanjali continue to grow and reach more people.” 
 Sumit Israni, Managing Director and Celebrity Hairdresser, Geetanjali Salon, said, “Chandigarh is an important market for us, with a growing interest in professional beauty, haircare and personalised salon experiences. The company is continuing to expand its restaurant footprint across existing and emerging markets, with a focus on improving customer access and convenience. The latest additions bring the business closer to its target milestone of 500 restaurants. Westlife Foodworld said its growth strategy combines restaurant expansion with improvements in customer experience, menu offerings and access to ordering channels.
 Amit Jatia, Chairperson of Westlife Foodworld Limited said, “ The results of the quarter reflect the strength of our strategy, the discipline of our execution and the enduring relevance of the McDonald's brand. The McDonald's app ecosystem crossed 58 million cumulative downloads, while monthly active users reached approximately 4.2 million.  Maheshwari has spent the past six years building Honasa's data and product capabilities, working across business intelligence, technology and product development. His new responsibilities will include turning these capabilities into scalable AI-powered systems to support decision-making, improve operational efficiency and streamline business processes.
 As Honasa expands its beauty and personal care portfolio, the company is investing in AI tools and automated workflows to simplify operations and help teams make decisions faster. It is also exploring agentic AI systems that can coordinate tasks and execute multi-step workflows under appropriate human supervision. The company aims to integrate AI into its day-to-day operations rather than limit its use to individual applications. Maheshwari's experience in data analytics and product development is expected to support the development and implementation of these systems across the organisation.
 Varun Alagh, Co-Founder and CEO of Honasa Consumer Limited said, “ Technology has always been an important enabler of our growth, and AI presents an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how we build and operate our business. Vipul’s strong foundation in data and product, along with his deep understanding of our business, makes him well positioned to shape and lead this journey. His elevation reflects our commitment to building leadership from within and investing in capabilities that will define our next phase of growth. ”
 The company's AI strategy includes developing workflows that automate repetitive tasks, connect business processes and support operational decisions. Its proposed agentic AI systems are intended to handle multiple steps within a workflow, with human oversight built into their implementation. These initiatives form part of Honasa's efforts to use technology to manage its expanding business and improve coordination across its functions.
 Vipul Maheshwari, Chief Product and Technology Officer at Honasa Consumer Limited said, “ AI and agentic systems represent a fundamental shift in how businesses will operate, moving from tools that provide information to intelligent systems that can execute workflows, connect decisions and drive outcomes. We are focused on developing intelligent workflows, enabling AI agents to support multi-step processes with the right guardrails, and embedding intelligence into everyday operations.  In his new position, Maheshwari will focus on developing AI-enabled systems that can be deployed across business functions. The company intends to use these capabilities to improve productivity, strengthen decision-making and support more efficient operations as its brand portfolio grows.

 Sabudana dishes emerged as the most ordered fasting food nationwide between October 17 and October 20, followed by Navratri vrat thalis, Singhara-based preparations, Kuttu and Rajgira specialities. Samak rice and Makhana dishes also featured among popular fasting options.

Mumbai and Bengaluru recorded strong demand for Sabudana Khichdi, with Pune and Jaipur also contributing to orders. 
 Complete festive meal combinations also attracted consumers. Navratri Special Vrat Thalis, particularly those served with Singhara Poori, were among the preferred options. Rajgira Poori and Aloo Hing three-course thalis also featured prominently, with Delhi, Bengaluru, Gurugram and Noida recording the highest demand. 
 A customer in Noida placed an order worth Rs 11,072 on October 17-18, including 13 units of Navratri Special Vrat Thali with Singhara Poori, making it one of the largest fasting-food orders recorded during the weekend. 
 Traditional sweets also saw higher demand during the four-day festive period. According to Swiggy, orders for traditional sweets increased by 36.4 percent between October 17 and October 20, 2026, compared with the corresponding festive period from September 29 to October 2, 2025. 
 While metropolitan cities such as Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi and Hyderabad recorded substantial demand, several emerging markets, including Patna, Dehradun, Jodhpur, Gaya and Thiruvananthapuram, also reported strong sweet orders. Among smaller cities and towns, Agartala, Shillong, Palwal and Bathinda recorded notable demand. 
 A Mumbai customer placed an order worth Rs 9,870 for assorted traditional sweets and Coffee Rasgulla Tiramisu, marking the highest-value rasgulla-related order recorded by Swiggy between October 17 and October 20, 2026.
